The classing of the ASK 562 replay on the 50 stored rounds found such false items in five forms.
      1. A combined tag ("[L1-L3]", "[L1-L2]", "[L1-L2-L3]") reads as [L1] if it holds 1, else as [L3] if it holds 3, else as its first layer (tag581, run on every line before inherit).
      2. A lead-in tag line that ends in ":" carries its tag onto a numbered list ("1." or "1)") as well as onto bullets; when the lead-in holds several tags the list takes [L1] if one of them is [L1], else [L3] if one is [L3], else the first tag. Every other tag line works as before.
      3. A bare chapter and verse ("24:16") takes the book of the last full reference on the same line, and only when the row of that derived verse is held (ref581). A time, a ratio or another book's chapter and verse is therefore not made a verse unless that exact row is on the sheet, and then the quotation must stand in that row.
      4. A trailing tag: a tag cluster after which only ".", ";", "," or the line end follow, outside parentheses, with the text before it ending in a closing quotation mark or ")" (or in a word, only when the tag ends the line and the word is not one of: no, not, nor, or, and, without, a, an, the, its, each, every). For each [L1] or [L3] in the cluster one extra read line is given to the verse reader for the sentence that ends at the tag (trail581); two verses under one trailing tag pair are both read. The round text is not changed. Lines that begin with [L4] are skipped.
      5. Order in the verse reader: tag581, inherit, ref581, trail581, canon566.
